hook: Two students explain why adding hydrogen makes more ammonia. One writes “the system shifts to relieve the stress.” The other writes “adding H₂ makes Q less than K, so the net reaction proceeds forward until Q equals K.” Only the second earns the point. This lesson is about writing the second answer every time.

prereq.q: A mixture has Q < K. Which way is the net reaction?
prereq.why: Q < K means too little product, so products form.

prereq.q: Adding a product to an equilibrium mixture makes it shift
options: toward whichever side has more moles
prereq.why: Le Châtelier: the system partly uses up what was added.

prereq.q: Which change alters K for a given reaction?

figure.caption: Concentration and volume changes move Q; temperature moves K. Either way Q ≠ K, and the system reacts until Q = K.

chain.cause: A concentration or the volume is changed
chain.effect: Q changes while K stays the same
K changes while Q stays the same at that instant

chain.cause: Q is now less than K
Q is now greater than K
chain.effect: the net reaction goes in reverse

chain.cause: The net reaction changes the concentrations
chain.effect: Q moves until Q = K again at a new equilibrium

ideas: Concentration and volume changes move Q; K stays fixed.
Temperature changes move K; Q is unchanged at that instant.
Then compare: Q < K net forward; Q > K net reverse; until Q = K.
A volume change shifts the equilibrium only if the gas exponents on the top and bottom of Q differ.

misconception.wrong: Adding a reactant increases K, and that is why more product forms.
misconception.right: Adding a reactant decreases Q (more on the bottom), so Q < K, and the net reaction goes forward until Q = K. K is unchanged; only temperature changes it.

summary: Every Le Châtelier shift can be justified by comparing Q with K. Changing a concentration, the volume or the pressure changes Q but not K; changing the temperature changes K but not Q at that instant. If Q is then less than K the net reaction goes forward, if greater it goes in reverse, until Q equals K again. Full-credit answers name what changed, give the comparison and the direction.
